hazards.hazard: Hot work (welding/grinding) on T-32 roof ignites flammable vapors venting from foul condensate tanks — flash fire/explosion in tank headspaces and vent header, roof collapse, personnel fatalities
equipment: T-31, T-32, T-33 foul condensate tanks
hazards.reason: Tanks stay in service with organic layer (methanol, turpentine) continuously generating flammable vapors; common vent header discharges at roofline directly at work area; scaffold puts ignition source in vapor path. Package lists hot work permit and fire extinguishers but no gas testing (LEL), vapor

hazards.hazard: 40-tonne crane lift over live white liquor line drops load or swings into line — line rupture sprays hot caustic NaOH/Na2S and releases H2S on riggers and below
hazards.reason: White liquor is hot caustic (NaOH/Na2S); Na2S hydrolyzes to H2S on release. Lifting plan and operator sign-off are listed but no mention of line isolation/blinding, exclusion zone, or H2S monitors for contractors (only operators issued). Crane size (40T) makes impact energy high.

hazards.hazard: Cutting 8-inch condensate line on T-32 roof without full purge/inert releases flammable vapor and hot organic liquid at ignition-source height — immediate ignition or toxic/flammable cloud on scaffold
hazards.reason: Line carries foul condensate with organics; tanks in service so line may hold pressure/vapors. LOTO and hot work permit listed but no mention of line draining, purging, inerting, or continuous vapor monitoring during cutting. Scaffold places workers in release zone.

hazards.hazard: Stripper feed pump opened for seal change with residual hot foul condensate (organics, H2S) in pump and suction line — caustic/organic spray, flammable vapor release, H2S exposure to maintenance crew
hazards.reason: Pump draws from T-33 (foul condensate with methanol, turpentine, organics). Package notes seal replacement but no drain/purge/inert procedure for pump opening. H2S monitors issued to operators only; maintenance crew may lack them. Eyewash/showers are mitigative only.

hazards.hazard: Common vent header blocked (ice, foam, organics) causes tank overpressure or vacuum collapse with scaffold crew on T-32 roof — roof failure, personnel fall into tank, flammable release
hazards.reason: Three tanks share one vent header to atmosphere at roofline; fixed cone roofs vulnerable to pressure/vacuum. No relief devices, blockage detection, or inspection mentioned. Scaffold crew on roof during Job 1 adds load and fall hazard if roof deforms.

hazards.hazard: Contractor orientation missed or inadequate — crews unaware of H2S, flammable vapors, caustic lines, roof hazards during all jobs — latent failure of all permit safeguards
hazards.reason: Orientation planned day 1 but no verification, content detail, or language assurance. All jobs rely on contractors recognizing hazards (flammables on roof, H2S at pump/white liquor, caustics, scaffold roof work). Missing orientation undermines every permit sign-off.

hazards.hazard: Common overflow line blocked — tank overfill spills flammable organic layer via vent header at roofline during hot work — ground-level flammable pool, fire escalation
hazards.reason: Three tanks share overflow; destination not described. No level alarms, high-level trips, or inspection mentioned. Overfill would discharge organic layer (methanol, turpentine) via vent header at roofline where hot work occurs. Safeguards only list overflow line existence.

hazards.hazard: Scaffold on T-32 fixed cone roof exceeds roof load capacity or lacks fall protection — crew falls into hot caustic/organic tank, drowning/chemical/thermal injury
hazards.reason: Fixed cone roof not designed for scaffold loads; tank contains hot foul condensate. Package mentions scaffold but no roof load verification, scaffold design review, fall arrest, or tank entry rescue plan. Operator sign-off is only control.

hazards.hazard: Steam header condensate pockets form during insulation repair; restart without drain causes water hammer — pipe rupture, steam/condensate whip, damage to adjacent white liquor/condensate lines
hazards.reason: Insulation repair (no hot work) cools header; condensate accumulates in low points. No mention of condensate drainage procedure or controlled warm-up. Adjacent white liquor line and condensate lines on same rack risk secondary damage from pipe whip.

hazards.hazard: White liquor line cools during crane lift or adjacent work — NaOH/Na2S crystallizes, blocks line; reheating causes overpressure rupture — delayed caustic/H2S release
hazards.reason: White liquor is hot caustic; cooling causes crystallization/blockage. Crane lift (Job 3) and steam header insulation (Job 4) may expose line to cooling. No temperature monitoring, heat tracing, or cool-down procedure mentioned. Rupture on reheating releases caustic + H2S.
